official.deadline_note: The call page publishes a single institutional deadline of 15 October 2026 at 15:00 Lisbon time; the Regulations state the submission window opens on 1 July and ends on 15 October each year, and no separate institutional deadline differing from the programme's is published.
official.application_cycle: 2027/28 academic year - applications open 1 July 2026 and close 15 October 2026; offers made from late January 2027
official.status_note: Open call: the call page shows a start date of 01 Jul 2026 and an end date of 15 Oct 2026 at 15:00 Lisbon time, for the academic year 2027/28, and states that fellowship offers will be made from late January of the following year.
official.tuition_coverage_note: No tuition is payable under this scheme: it funds a research residency at the Institute's premises rather than enrolment in a degree programme, and the published components of the fellowship are travel expenses, travel and health insurance, a monthly stipend, and a partial accommodation allowance.
benefits: An individual office, with access to seminar rooms, electronic resources, on-campus restaurants where coffee and lunch are generally available on weekdays, and borrowing privileges from university libraries in the Lisbon area and from the Gulbenkian Art Library
A formal letter confirming the fellowship and its conditions for visa purposes, and help in finding accommodation, and schools for accompanying children, when required
eligibility: Applications are eligible if submitted by individuals, including professionals associated with academia either independently or through formal affiliation, emeritus professors, other professionals not linked to academia, and artists
Applications are accepted in any scientific field, provided that the work to be developed does not require laboratory or experimental procedures and is not primarily practice- or application-oriented
Most applicants hold a PhD, but this is not a formal requirement
No knowledge of Portuguese is required and there are no restrictions of nationality
Candidates who have received a Gulbenkian Institute for Advanced Study Fellowship within the last five years are excluded
requirements: Up to 15 fellowships will be awarded each year, with a minimum individual duration of three months and a maximum of eight months

Fellowships are preferably awarded for the full academic year, 15 September through 15 May (eight months), though three-month (fall semester) and four-month (spring semester) fellowships may be considered
Fellowships require continuous residency; short absences may be exceptionally allowed
The Foundation awards only one fellowship per successful candidate
Each fellow is expected to conduct at least one lunchtime presentation during the stay; weekday lunch attendance is recommended but not mandatory
The Institute expects to award up to 15 fellowships each year, with the final number depending on the actual duration of individual fellowships
documents: A brief description of the proposed activities; the FAQ advises that the proposal should not exceed three pages and should outline the research project, including its main themes, scholarly context, novelty, and the objectives for the stay at the GIAS
Names of two individuals who may be contacted for references
After selection, due-diligence documents for selected candidates: proof of bank account ownership, copy of an identification document, and the full address of permanent residence
selection_criteria: The innovative nature of the candidate's work proposal (60%)

Applications are assessed through a competitive international process in which the quality and originality of the proposed work, in keeping with the Institute's spirit and intellectual environment, are the central considerations

Applications are assessed, prioritised and selected by the Advisory Board of the Gulbenkian Institute for Advanced Study, subject to the final decision of the Executive Board of the Calouste Gulbenkian Foundation, which is not subject to appeal
coverage: The amount of the fellowship is set when the application is selected, and the sum of the fellowships awarded each year may not exceed the amount budgeted for that year; the determination considers the length of the candidate's stay and their curriculum
application_method: Submit an individual application through the MyGulbenkian portal
The application must be accompanied by a Curriculum Vitae, a brief description of the proposed activities, and the names of two individuals who may be contacted for references
Referees will be contacted directly by the Institute and requested to submit their letters of recommendation via the MyGulbenkian platform; reference letters sent by email are not accepted
Once submitted, the application and all uploaded documents are visible in the 'Applications' section of the applicant's MyGulbenkian account; no automatic confirmation email is sent

Acceptance of support is confirmed by signing the corresponding contract or fellowship award agreement, which may be signed with a qualified electronic signature and submitted electronically, or signed by hand and sent by post
official.application_route: Individual online application through the MyGulbenkian portal, submitted between 1 July and 15 October at 15:00 Lisbon time, with a CV, a project description and two referee names.
official.study_mode: Continuous residency at the Institute's premises in Lisbon, with minimal regular obligations
official.citizenship_residency: No restrictions of nationality; no knowledge of Portuguese required; no specific academic degree is a formal requirement
official.international_eligibility: International academics are explicitly eligible, and there are no restrictions of nationality
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Any scientific field is accepted, provided the work does not require laboratory or experimental procedures and is not primarily practice- or application-oriented
official.research_requirement: A brief description of the proposed activities, of no more than three pages, covering the main themes of the research project, its scholarly context, novelty, and the objectives for the stay at the GIAS
official.duration: Minimum three months and maximum eight months per residency; preferably awarded for the full academic year, 15 September through 15 May
official.description: The Gulbenkian Institute for Advanced Study was established by the Calouste Gulbenkian Foundation to enable internationally renowned academics to carry out research of interest to them for limited periods of time in a stimulating and unconstrained intellectual environment. Fellows are encouraged to pursue projects of their own choosing in a setting designed to encourage reflection, concentration, and exchange, within a vibrant intellectual community drawn from a wide range of disciplines, backgrounds, and nationalities.

applicant_utility.summary: No stipend figure is published anywhere: the amount is fixed only after selection, weighing the length of your stay against your curriculum, so plan your finances as if the award value is unknown until the contract arrives. The published weighting is 60% on the innovative nature of the work proposal and 40% on the CV, so a tightly argued three-page project carries more weight than a long publication list. Applications close at 15 October 2026, 15:00 Lisbon time, through the MyGulbenkian portal, with offers going out from late January 2027. Up to 15 fellowships are on offer for 2027/28, and the Institute prefers a continuous eight-month residency from 15 September to 15 May.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Mid-career and established non-laboratory scholars, writers, philosophers and artists who can clear three to eight uninterrupted months for Lisbon and can frame a genuinely self-directed project.
application_readiness_checklist: Rewrite the project description to the FAQ's three-page ceiling and structure it around the four things the Institute asks for: main themes, scholarly context, novelty, and objectives for the stay.
Alert both referees early that GIAS contacts them directly and collects letters through MyGulbenkian only, and that emailed letters are rejected outright.
Rehearse how the CV earns 40% of the score: name the outputs that show a sustained research programme rather than padding the list.
Block out the calendar before applying: a preferred stay starts 15 September, offers go out from late January, and results must be settled by 15 April 2027.
Have the post-selection due-diligence pack ready (proof of bank account ownership, ID copy, full permanent-residence address) so signing the award agreement does not stall.
common_rejection_risks: A project that reads as needing laboratory, experimental or field infrastructure, or as practice-led and applied rather than inquiry-led.
A previous GIAS residency within the last five years, which is an automatic exclusion under the Regulations, not merely a scoring penalty.
A missing mandatory item at submission, or referees who never file through MyGulbenkian because nobody warned them the email route is closed.
A proposal that runs past three pages or that describes the applicant's past work instead of what will be done in Lisbon.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Housing beyond the partial accommodation allowance, daily living costs in Lisbon above the stipend, visa and residence-permit fees, relocation and shipping, any conference or separate fieldwork travel, and school fees for accompanying children, since the award covers only travel to and from Lisbon, insurance, the stipend, and part of the accommodation.
document_audit: You upload only three things: the CV, the project description, and two referee names. The reference letters themselves are filed by the referees through MyGulbenkian, so they are outside your control.
The three-page proposal limit is a real ceiling, not guidance: set your word count before drafting rather than trimming afterwards.
Proof of bank account ownership is requested only after selection, and it must evidence an account you own, not a salary or affiliation letter.

The Institute sits in the Gulbenkian Foundation building in downtown Lisbon now and moves to a restored palace in Oeiras by autumn 2029, so do not assume the 2027/28 address equals the permanent campus.
alerts: The 15 October 2026, 15:00 Lisbon deadline is a hard portal cut-off in the awarding body's own terms, and the clock is Lisbon time, not your own timezone.
The residency must be continuous, with only exceptional short absences, so clashing teaching terms, grant deliverables or caring responsibilities are a genuine disqualifier in practice.
There is no confirmation email after submitting: check the 'Applications' section of your MyGulbenkian account to verify that every document uploaded.
The award is a grant, not employment income, and is not subject to Portuguese withholding, but it may still be taxable in your country of residence.
Fellowships are not renewable, and a former fellow must wait at least five years since their last residency before reapplying.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Apply individually through MyGulbenkian, upload the CV, the project description and two referee names before 15 October 2026 at 15:00 Lisbon time, then monitor the 'Applications' section of your account since no automatic confirmation email is issued.
